title: Borehole Water Pumps Kenya | DripTech Eco Flow
description: Submersible and solar borehole pumps for irrigation in Kenya. Compare pump options for your borehole depth and yield and get help sizing the system.
h1: Borehole water pumps for irrigation
intro: Once a borehole is drilled and its yield known, the next decision is matching a pump to that depth and yield. DripTech Eco Flow supplies the pumps, controllers and fittings for borehole-fed irrigation — not the drilling itself, which is a specialised hydrogeological service.

sections.heading: Matching a pump to your borehole
paragraphs: A pump sized below your borehole's actual yield runs the risk of dry-running and early failure, while an oversized pump wastes money. Your driller's yield test result and the depth to water are the key inputs.

Submersible electric pumps suit boreholes with reliable grid power; solar submersible pumps suit sites without it, at the cost of pumping only during usable daylight hours unless paired with battery storage.

title: Irrigation Water Storage Tanks Kenya | DripTech
description: Water storage tanks sized for drip and sprinkler irrigation in Kenya. Compare tank sizes against your plot size, pump output and buffer requirements.
h1: Water storage tanks for farm irrigation
intro: A storage tank buffers supply between your water source and the field, smoothing out pump downtime, solar pumping hours, or an intermittent municipal or borehole supply. Sizing it against your daily water demand avoids both running dry mid-irrigation and paying for capacity you never use.

sections.heading: Sizing a tank to your system
paragraphs: A useful starting point is your system's daily water requirement across all beds or zones, plus a buffer for the hours your pump or supply is unavailable — overnight for a solar pump, for example.
Tank position also matters: a raised or elevated tank can supply a basic gravity-fed drip layout without a pump, while a ground-level tank needs a pump to reach field pressure.

bullets: Daily water demand across your plot size and crop
Buffer hours needed if your pump or supply is intermittent

Many greenhouse growers also fertigate — feeding nutrients through the same drip system — which needs a compatible dosing setup alongside the dripline itself.

description: Fertigation systems for Kenyan farms and greenhouses: feed fertiliser through drip irrigation for even nutrient delivery. Compare dosing equipment.
h1: Fertigation systems for drip irrigation
intro: Fertigation feeds water-soluble fertiliser through the same drip system that waters the crop, so every plant on the line gets a consistent dose instead of uneven hand application. It works alongside an existing drip layout rather than replacing it.

sections.heading: How fertigation fits into a drip system
paragraphs: A fertigation setup injects a measured amount of dissolved fertiliser into the irrigation line, usually just after the filter and before the line splits into zones, so dosing stays consistent across the field or greenhouse.
Getting the dosing rate right depends on your crop's nutrient program and how often you irrigate — this is worth confirming before buying equipment sized for a different schedule.

description: Compare drip and sprinkler irrigation in Kenya by crop layout, soil, wind, water pressure, maintenance and budget before choosing a farm system.
h1: Drip vs sprinkler irrigation: how to choose in Kenya
intro: Drip and sprinkler systems apply water differently, and neither is automatically best for every farm. The right option depends on crop arrangement, soil, wind exposure, water quality, available flow, labour and the way the field is managed.

sections.heading: When drip irrigation may fit
paragraphs: Drip systems deliver water through emitters near the crop rows or root zone. They can suit row crops, many vegetable beds, orchards and some greenhouse layouts when filtration, pressure and maintenance are handled correctly.
Dripline spacing, emitter flow, filtration and line length must match the field design. Blockages and poor pressure management can reduce uniformity, so routine checks matter.

sections.heading: When sprinklers may fit
paragraphs: Sprinklers distribute water over an area and can suit crops or layouts that benefit from broader coverage. Their performance depends on operating pressure, sprinkler spacing, wind and the application rate relative to soil intake.
Sprinkler systems need compatible pumps, pipes and fittings. Wind and evaporation can affect application, so site conditions and crop needs should be assessed before selection.

description: Plan greenhouse irrigation in Kenya with guidance on dripline layout, filtration, fertigation, pressure and system maintenance.
h1: Greenhouse irrigation systems for Kenyan growers
intro: Greenhouse irrigation should fit the crop rows, bed arrangement, water source and growing system. A well-planned setup makes it easier to manage delivery, inspect components and maintain consistent operation.

sections.heading: Design around the greenhouse layout
paragraphs: Measure the greenhouse, beds and crop rows, then confirm water-source flow and pressure. The layout determines the number and length of drip lines and how the greenhouse should be divided into zones.
Choose emitter spacing and discharge for the crop arrangement, soil or growing medium and equipment specifications. Keep access for flushing, filter cleaning and repairs.

sections.heading: Plan filtration and fertigation
bullets: Filter selected for the water source and emitters
Dripline, connectors, valves and flush points
Pump and pipe capacity matched to required flow
Compatible fertigation equipment when needed
Pressure checks and a routine maintenance plan

sections.heading: Avoid one-size-fits-all schedules
paragraphs: Greenhouse conditions can change with temperature, ventilation, crop stage and growing medium. Base irrigation decisions on appropriate crop guidance and monitoring, not a fixed schedule copied from another greenhouse.
Share the greenhouse dimensions, crop, water source and location with DripTech Eco Flow for help planning equipment.

title: Irrigation System Cost Kenya: Price Factors | DripTech
description: Understand what affects irrigation system cost in Kenya, from acreage and crop layout to pumps, filtration, pipes, installation and delivery.
h1: How much does an irrigation system cost in Kenya?
intro: Irrigation costs vary by field layout, crop, water source and equipment. A meaningful quote should list the components and installation scope instead of relying on acreage alone.

sections.heading: What determines the total cost?
bullets: Area, crop spacing and the number of irrigation lines
Drip, sprinkler or other application method
Pump, power source, water storage and required pressure
Filters, mainline, submain, valves, connectors and fittings
Site conditions, installation labour, delivery and commissioning

sections.heading: Compare quotes fairly
paragraphs: Check whether each quote includes the same items, quantities, installation work, testing and support. A low headline price may exclude the pump, filtration, fittings or installation that the farm still needs.
Current product prices and stock can change. Use the live catalogue for listed items and request a farm-specific bill of materials before relying on a final project budget.

sections.heading: Request a practical estimate
paragraphs: Send your crop, acreage, water source, location and whether you need installation. DripTech Eco Flow can use those details to discuss a system scope and the equipment required.

title: One-Acre Drip Irrigation System in Kenya | DripTech
description: Plan a one-acre drip irrigation system in Kenya with guidance on crop spacing, water supply, filters, pipes, zones and kit selection.
h1: Planning a drip irrigation system for one acre
intro: A one-acre system is not a single fixed kit. Crop spacing, number of rows, field shape, water source and available pressure determine the quantities and system layout.

sections.heading: Information needed before sizing
bullets: Crop and row or bed spacing
Field shape, slope and distance from the water source
Available water flow, storage and pump details
Soil and water quality considerations
Whether installation and delivery are required

sections.heading: Typical system components
paragraphs: A complete design may include driplines, mainline and submain pipe, a filter, valves, connectors, flush points and a pump or tank connection where needed. The quantities and specifications should be calculated from the actual layout.
The field may need to be divided into zones if the available flow or pressure cannot support the entire area at once. Confirm sizing against the product specifications before purchase.

sections.heading: Get a bill of materials for your acre
paragraphs: Share your crop, row spacing, water source and location with DripTech Eco Flow. This makes it possible to discuss a realistic parts list rather than guessing quantities from acreage alone.

title: How to Choose Dripline Spacing in Kenya | DripTech
description: Learn what affects dripline emitter spacing and discharge in Kenya, including crop layout, soil, line length, pressure and filtration.
h1: How to choose dripline and emitter spacing
intro: Dripline selection is about more than roll length. Emitter spacing, discharge, operating pressure, line length and soil influence how water spreads along the crop row.

sections.heading: Match spacing to crop and soil
paragraphs: Start with crop spacing, bed width and the intended root-zone coverage. Soil texture and the way water moves through the soil also affect whether a particular emitter spacing is appropriate.
Closely spaced emitters are not automatically best for every crop, and wider spacing is not always suitable. Confirm the choice against the crop layout, soil and manufacturer guidance.

sections.heading: Check flow, pressure and filtration
bullets: Emitter discharge and operating-pressure range
Maximum practical line length for the chosen product
Available flow and pressure at the field
Filter type and capacity for the water source
Connectors, flush points and compatibility with mainline

sections.heading: Confirm before ordering
paragraphs: Send the crop, row spacing, bed dimensions, water source and approximate field size to DripTech Eco Flow. Those details help narrow the options and avoid choosing a roll based on spacing alone.

title: Irrigation Pump Sizing Kenya: Flow & Head | DripTech
description: Learn the main inputs for irrigation pump sizing in Kenya, including required flow, total head, water source, pipe losses and power supply.
h1: How to size a pump for farm irrigation
intro: Pump selection should be based on the flow the irrigation system needs and the total head the pump must overcome. Choosing by horsepower alone can lead to a system that does not deliver the required flow or pressure.

sections.heading: Inputs needed for pump selection
bullets: Required flow rate for the zones operating at one time
Vertical lift and delivery height
Pressure required by the irrigation equipment
Pipe lengths, diameters and friction losses
Water-source depth, yield and available power supply

sections.heading: Match the pump to the application
paragraphs: Drip and sprinkler systems can have different flow and pressure requirements. Borehole pumps also need to be matched to the water level, borehole yield and delivery conditions; a borehole yield test is an important input.
For solar pumping, consider daily water volume, available sunlight, pumping window and any storage needed. Confirm calculations with the pump performance curve and a qualified installer.

sections.heading: Get sizing help
paragraphs: Share the water source, depth or lift, field size, irrigation method and required flow if known. DripTech Eco Flow can help identify the information needed to compare suitable pump options.

title: Irrigation System Maintenance in Kenya | DripTech
description: Practical irrigation maintenance checks for farms in Kenya, including filters, leaks, blocked emitters, pressure, valves and seasonal inspection.
h1: Irrigation system maintenance checklist
intro: Routine maintenance helps farmers find leaks, blockages and pressure problems before they disrupt watering. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for each component and adapt checks to the water source and system design.

sections.heading: Regular checks for drip systems
bullets: Inspect and clean filters as directed by the manufacturer
Look for leaks, damaged connectors and loose fittings
Check line ends and flush according to the system instructions
Look for blocked emitters or uneven water delivery
Monitor pressure and confirm valves operate correctly

sections.heading: Sprinkler, pump and storage checks
paragraphs: Check sprinkler heads for damage or obstruction and confirm spacing and pressure remain appropriate. Inspect pump connections, controls and storage arrangements according to the equipment manual; isolate power safely before servicing.
If pressure changes, leaks persist or equipment behaves unusually, stop and have the system assessed rather than making adjustments beyond your training.

sections.heading: Need help troubleshooting?
paragraphs: When contacting a technician, provide the water source, equipment type, symptoms, photos if safe to take, and any recent changes. DripTech Eco Flow can help discuss product compatibility and irrigation support.

title: Irrigation Troubleshooting Guide Kenya | DripTech Eco Flow
description: Diagnose common drip and sprinkler irrigation problems in Kenya, from blocked emitters and uneven watering to leaks, filters, pressure and pump issues.
h1: Irrigation troubleshooting guide for Kenyan farms
intro: When an irrigation system stops delivering water evenly, check the basics before replacing equipment. This guide helps you narrow down common drip and sprinkler problems safely, identify what information to collect, and know when a technician should inspect the system.

sections.heading: Start with these checks
bullets: Check whether the water source has enough water and the pump or supply is operating normally
Inspect the filter and clean it according to the manufacturer's instructions
Look for leaks, kinked pipes, closed valves and disconnected fittings
Compare water delivery at the beginning and end of lines
Turn the system off and isolate pressure before opening fittings or servicing equipment

sections.heading: Choose the problem that matches your system
paragraphs: Use the focused guides for blocked drippers, weak sprinkler coverage, leaks and pressure or pump problems. Symptoms can have several causes, so avoid replacing a pump or changing pressure settings based on one observation alone.

sections.heading: When to request technical support
paragraphs: If the system still performs unevenly after basic checks, share photos or a short video, the pump or filter model if known, the water source, and which zones are affected. DripTech Eco Flow can help assess the likely cause and discuss service options.

title: Blocked Drippers & Uneven Watering Kenya | DripTech
description: Learn what to check when drip emitters block or crop rows receive uneven water, including filters, flushing, pressure and line layout.
h1: How to troubleshoot blocked drippers and uneven watering
intro: Blocked emitters and uneven watering can result from sediment, biological growth, mineral deposits, leaks or pressure differences. Identify where the problem occurs before deciding which component needs attention.

sections.heading: Find out whether the problem is local or across the field
bullets: If only a few emitters are affected, inspect that section for kinks, damage or local blockage
If many lines are affected, inspect the filter, water source and supply pressure
Compare the first and last parts of a line to identify a possible distribution issue
Check for leaks and disconnected fittings that divert flow

sections.heading: Clean and flush carefully
paragraphs: Follow the filter and dripline manufacturer's cleaning and flushing instructions. Isolate the system and release pressure before opening end caps or fittings. Do not mix cleaning chemicals or apply acid treatments unless the equipment guidance and qualified advice specifically support it.
If the issue returns quickly, the filtration setup or source-water quality may not suit the emitters. A technician can help identify the likely cause before you buy replacement parts.

sections.heading: Prevent the same issue recurring
bullets: Use filtration appropriate to the source water and emitter specifications
Inspect and clean filters at the recommended interval
Provide accessible line ends for flushing where the design requires them
Keep records of when blockage starts and which zones are affected

title: Low Irrigation Pressure & Weak Sprinklers Kenya | DripTech
description: Troubleshoot weak sprinkler throw and low irrigation pressure by checking supply, leaks, filters, pipe sizing and pump specifications.
h1: Troubleshooting low pressure and weak sprinkler coverage
intro: Weak sprinkler throw or low flow at the far end of a field can have several causes. Check the supply and distribution system methodically; a larger pump is not always the right fix.

sections.heading: Check the water supply and system condition
bullets: Confirm the source has enough water during irrigation
Inspect filters, valves and pipework for blockage or accidental restriction
Look for leaks and damaged connections
Check whether too many sprinklers or zones are operating at once
Compare the installed sprinkler requirements with the available operating pressure and flow

sections.heading: Verify pump and pipe sizing
paragraphs: Pump selection depends on required flow at the total dynamic head, including elevation and friction losses. Read the pump curve and sprinkler specifications rather than relying on the motor power rating alone. Pipe diameter, line length and fittings also affect pressure losses.
Do not adjust pressure controls beyond equipment limits. If pressure remains low, have the pump, layout and measured operating conditions checked before replacing equipment.

sections.heading: Information to collect for a diagnosis
bullets: Pump make and model, if available
Number and type of sprinklers operating together
Approximate pipe sizes and longest run
Water source and elevation difference
Where pressure or coverage becomes weak

title: Irrigation Pipe Leaks & Fittings Kenya | DripTech
description: Find common causes of irrigation pipe leaks, loose connectors and damaged fittings, with safe checks before repairs or replacement.
h1: How to troubleshoot irrigation leaks and damaged fittings
intro: Leaks waste water and can reduce delivery to other parts of an irrigation system. Identify the damaged section and relieve pressure before inspecting or repairing pipes and fittings.

sections.heading: Locate the leak and isolate the affected section
bullets: Switch off the pump or water supply and safely release system pressure
Inspect joints, valves, connectors and visible pipe sections
Look for cracked fittings, loose connections, damaged seals or pipe punctures
Check whether movement, sunlight exposure or unsupported pipework may have contributed
After repair, restart gradually and inspect the joint for leaks

sections.heading: Choose compatible replacement parts
paragraphs: Match the pipe diameter, pressure rating, connection type and material. A fitting that looks similar may not seal correctly or withstand the system's operating pressure. Use components within the manufacturer's specifications and seek qualified help for buried, high-pressure or repeatedly failing sections.

sections.heading: Reduce repeat failures
bullets: Support exposed pipework where needed
Avoid forcing mismatched threads or connectors
Protect equipment from avoidable impact and excessive pressure
Include valves and joints in routine inspections

title: Drip Tape vs Dripline in Kenya: Buying Guide | DripTech
description: Compare drip tape and dripline for Kenyan farms: wall thickness, emitter spacing, durability, filtration and pressure, and how to choose for your crop.
h1: Drip tape vs dripline: which is right for your farm?
intro: Drip tape and dripline both deliver water near crop roots, but they are not interchangeable in every field. The better choice depends on crop spacing, season length, pressure, filtration, installation method and how often the lines will be moved.

sections.heading: What is drip tape?
paragraphs: Drip tape is generally a thin-walled irrigation tube designed for row crops and planned seasonal use. It can be a practical option where lines are laid out in crop beds and operating pressure stays within the product specification.
Tape products differ in wall thickness, emitter spacing, flow rate and pressure limits. Check the manufacturer's data rather than assuming every tape roll has the same performance or service life.

sections.heading: What is dripline?
paragraphs: Dripline is a broad term for tubing used in drip irrigation; many products have built-in emitters and are available in different wall thicknesses and emitter designs. Some are intended for repeated or longer-term installation, but actual durability depends on the specific product and operating conditions.

For orchards, greenhouses and vegetable rows, compare the emitter type, spacing, flow rate, tube diameter, pressure range and compatibility with the proposed layout. The label alone does not tell you whether a product is suitable.

sections.heading: Compare the specifications before buying
bullets: Wall thickness and stated service conditions
Emitter spacing and discharge rate per emitter or metre
Recommended operating pressure and allowable pressure variation
Filtration requirements for the water source
Tube diameter, connectors, end fittings and flushing method
UV exposure, handling, storage and whether lines will be reused
Supplier warranty and availability of matching repair fittings

sections.heading: Which option suits different farms?
paragraphs: For short-season row crops, a suitable thin-wall tape may meet the design need when the layout, water quality and pressure are controlled. For repeated use or installations where lines remain in place, compare thicker-wall dripline products and their manufacturer specifications.

For orchards or widely spaced plants, individual emitters or a purpose-designed dripline layout may be more appropriate than choosing tape solely because it is cheaper per roll. The required number of lines per row depends on root-zone coverage, soil, crop stage and irrigation design.

sections.heading: Filtration, pressure and maintenance matter
paragraphs: Both tape and dripline can clog if the water contains particles, algae or other material that the filtration system does not remove. Select filtration according to the water source and emitter specifications, then maintain and flush the system as directed.

Too much or too little pressure can create uneven application or damage components. Use the manufacturer's pressure range and check the actual flow and pressure under operating conditions before expanding the system.

sections.heading: How to choose the right product in Kenya
paragraphs: Before requesting a quotation, note your crop, planted area, row and plant spacing, water source, available flow, elevation changes and whether the system is seasonal or permanent. Share product labels or photos if you are comparing two rolls.
DripTech Eco Flow can help discuss available irrigation components and the information needed for a farm-specific quotation. Confirm current stock, specifications and prices before ordering.

title: Irrigation Filter & Pump Problems Kenya | DripTech
description: Troubleshoot common irrigation filter and pump symptoms, including repeated filter blockage, reduced flow and supply interruptions.
h1: Troubleshooting irrigation filter and pump problems
intro: Filters and pumps perform different jobs: filtration protects downstream equipment, while the pump or source must provide the flow and pressure the system needs. Symptoms should be checked against both components and the pipe layout.

sections.heading: If the filter blocks repeatedly
bullets: Check whether source water contains sand, organic matter or other suspended material
Clean the filter only as described by the manufacturer
Check that the filter type and rating are appropriate for the source and emitters
Investigate whether the intake or source has changed

sections.heading: If the pump flow is reduced or stops
bullets: Confirm the source has adequate water and the intake is not obstructed
Check for visible leaks, closed valves and blocked filters
Record any alarms or unusual changes without opening electrical or pressurised equipment
Compare the pump model and operating conditions with its manufacturer guidance

sections.heading: Know when to call a qualified technician
paragraphs: Electrical faults, borehole pump removal, persistent loss of prime, overheating, abnormal noise or pressure-vessel problems require appropriate qualified service. Do not open electrical equipment or dismantle a pump while it is powered or pressurised.
Share the pump model, water source, symptom, affected zones and recent changes to help the support team understand the issue.
